model_interpretation.claim: The 16-byte SSE2 prefix scan can skip long initial ASCII runs, while the 8-byte word checks after the first mixed vector may skip later complete ASCII blocks that scalar suffix decoding would inspect byte by byte. The additional masks and mixed-block decoding may instead cost more on short or dense non-ASCII inputs. The combined program is unmeasured and must beat the parent's 39.978 µs mean; no additive gain is assumed.

model_interpretation.claim: The SSE2 path already classifies starters and continuation requirements across 16-byte blocks, but performs several SIMD comparisons to validate restricted second-byte ranges. Checking those ranges scalarly only for E0, ED, F0, or F4 starter lanes may reduce per-block SIMD work when those starters are infrequent. Lane-15 checks remain deferred across the block boundary, and the existing scalar validator remains the fallback/control. This is an unmeasured hybrid; the official mixed-width n=65536 timing will determine whether it helps.

model_interpretation.claim: This distinct hybrid tests whether SIMD can capture later ASCII spans without paying for a SIMD restart after each decoded code point: skip complete 16-byte ASCII vectors, then strictly decode a 64-byte window after a mixed vector before resuming SIMD. It may help if the official mixed-width input has later ASCII spans; otherwise the scalar windows may add overhead. The fallback begins at a code-point boundary and validates the first high-bit byte rather than assuming it is a lead. No speedup is claimed.

model_interpretation.claim: Baseline T3 measurements put the original decoder at 49.623 µs and predicate aggregation at 49.545 µs, while the measured shared-loop and table-DFA variants were slower. This distinct pure-scalar test replaces per-width validation branches in the main loop with masked predicates and arithmetic width advancement, using a bounded four-byte lookahead and the scalar decoder for the final short tail. It may reduce control-flow dependencies, but redundant lookahead loads for short sequences may erase any gain; the controller must measure it on the official mixed-width n=65536 workload.
